new_entities.name: PCSK9 inhibitor therapy after acute coronary syndrome
new_entities.description: Use of a PCSK9 inhibitor after acute coronary syndrome in addition to maximally tolerated statin therapy.

new_entities.name: Major adverse cardiovascular events
new_entities.description: Composite cardiovascular outcomes such as cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, unstable angina hospitalization, or repeat revascularization.

edges.effect_quant: ACS-focused meta-analysis found PCSK9 inhibition reduced MACE overall (RR 0.87). In ODYSSEY OUTCOMES, alirocumab lowered the primary composite endpoint from 11.1% to 9.5% after recent ACS (HR 0.85), and total-event analysis showed fewer recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular and fatal events with continued therapy.
edges.population: adults within months of acute coronary syndrome who remain at elevated lipid-driven residual risk despite high-intensity or maximally tolerated statin therapy
edges.mechanism: Profound LDL lowering after plaque rupture likely stabilizes residual high-risk coronary plaque and reduces recurrent ischemic events beyond statin therapy alone.
edges.summary: This is a clean secondary-prevention lipid-escalation signal, especially in higher-risk or higher-LDL post-ACS patients. The benefit is clinically meaningful but still modest in absolute terms, so it is best targeted to those with the most residual risk.
edges.caveats: Much of the hard-outcome evidence comes from alirocumab-rich datasets rather than equally mature outcomes for every agent and every post-ACS timing strategy. Cost, injection burden, and baseline LDL level still matter for real-world use.

evidence.notes: Efficacy and safety of proprotein convertase subtilisin kexin type (PCSK9) inhibitors in patients with acute coronary syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: MACE with PCSK9 inhibitors versus control in ACS studies

evidence.citation: Schwartz GG et al 2018 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: Alirocumab and Cardiovascular Outcomes after Acute Coronary Syndrome. ODYSSEY OUTCOMES.

effect_quant.comparator: primary composite MACE endpoint in ODYSSEY OUTCOMES with alirocumab versus placebo after ACS

evidence.citation: Szarek M et al 2019 J Am Coll Cardiol
evidence.notes: Alirocumab Reduces Total Nonfatal Cardiovascular and Fatal Events: The ODYSSEY OUTCOMES Trial.

effect_quant.comparator: total nonfatal cardiovascular events in the prespecified ODYSSEY OUTCOMES total-event analysis with alirocumab versus placebo
